newsitem.title: UK: NatWest forms new wealth management arm.
newsitem.headline: NatWest forms new wealth management arm.

text.p: Britain's NatWest Group said on Thursday it was forming a new business grouping, NatWest Wealth Management, to unite its fund managment, life insurance, venture capital and private banking operations.

NatWest said in a statement the unit would bring together asset management company Gartmore, life insurance and pensions unit NatWest Life and Investment Services and NatWest Ventures. Private banking unit Coutts Group will join the new arm in January 1998 following completion of Coutts' restructuring.

NatWest Wealth Management will have funds under management in excess of 60 billion pounds ($98.03 billion). The group said it was formed to develop National Westminster Bank Plc's ambitions in what it called the "highly attractive markets for private banking, long-term savings and investments."

Paul Myners, chairman of Gartmore, Britain's fifth-largest fund manager, which NatWest acquired in April 1996, will be chief executive of the new unit from April 1 and will report directly to NatWest Group chief executive Derek Wanless.

"NatWest Markets' stewardship of Gartmore was key to the successful integration of our asset management activities and the creation for the group of a first class investment management capability. Now that has been completed we are ready to place Gartmore in closer proximity to other group businesses directly involved in wealth management activities," Wanless said.

Myners said the businesses in the new group were already well established and successful and together represented a "substantial force in the provision of long-term savings and investment products." ($1=.6120 Pound)
